demonstrated_gap: It is the only tool surveyed that both measures a skill and improves it behind a held-out gate. Its paper reports gains on GPT-5.5 of +19.1 points inside Claude Code and +24.8 inside Codex, and says it is best or tied on all 52 (model, benchmark, harness) cells; an edit is accepted only if it strictly improves the held-out validation score. The main branch adds an unreleased paired A/B evalkit (McNemar test plus percentile-bootstrap confidence intervals on a fixed task manifest). It stays compare-only for six reasons. (1) The gains are on public benchmarks, not this repository's tasks. (2) Features after 0.2.0 need a source install from main. (3) SkillOpt-Sleep harvests local Claude Code/Codex transcripts and states 'Outbound prompts are not currently guaranteed to be secret-free'. (4) Adopting optimized text would leave pinned upstream skills locally modified, which the skills installer refuses without --force. (5) SkillsBench found that self-generated skills give no benefit on average. (6) The precondition from the 2026-09-22 sweep, a frozen held-out fixture, is still not met.
comparison_that_would_overturn: First build a frozen claude plugin eval suite for search-first and iterative-retrieval. Compare the optimized text against the pinned text on held-out cases, three runs per arm. Adopt only if the paired McNemar test gives p < 0.05 in favor of the optimized text, tokens rise by no more than 10%, and no edit falls outside the skill folder. Otherwise keep the upstream text.
